title: Naturality of completed purity and support comparison
statement: Let $k_0$ be a finite field of characteristic $p$, let $k$ be its fixed algebraic closure, and fix a prime $\ell\ne p$ and a finite coefficient extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$, with ring of integers $\mathcal O_E$, as in [def-pur-conventions]. Let $X_0,Y_0$ be separated finite-type $k_0$-schemes, $f_0:X_0\to Y_0$ a separated finite-type morphism, and $X,Y,f$ their geometric base changes. Suppose $f$ is smooth of pure relative dimension $d\ge0$. Fix a compactification $c_0$ of $f_0$ and the specified exceptional coefficient system $S$, with the actual comparisons of [def-pur-weil-equivariance-data]. Let $\mathcal C_T=D^b_{ctf}(T,\mathcal O_E)$ be the derived-complete finite-Tor category, $P=Lg_Y^*$, $Q=Lg_X^*$, $H=Lf^*(-)(d)[2d]$, and $F\dashv G$ the specified constructible adjunction. Let $\Gamma_K:HK\simeq GK$ be integralGamma, the fixed canonical trace-transpose integral purity, and $B_M:PFM\simeq FQM$ be integralBeta, the specified completed proper/open exchange in those coordinates. For every integral arrow $a:K\to L$ one has $\Gamma_K\,G(a)=H(a)\,\Gamma_L$. For every integral arrow $v:M\to N$ on $X$ one has $P(F(v))\,B_N=B_M\,F(Q(v))$. These equations are in the actual completed full subcategories; no strict Weil datum is assumed.

proof.text: Use [det-sp-normalized-equivalence] to reduce every integral morphism to a morphism of its entire normalized tower. Naturality in [det-sp-tower-gamma] is an equality of whole-tower morphisms. Apply total derived inverse limit and the pullback, tensor and source comparisons of [lem-pur-integral-geometric-comparison-realization]. The counit-preserving right-adjoint comparison and [lem-pur-tower-trace-purity-comparison] identify the realized components with the specified trace-transpose integralGamma. Naturality of the reconstruction units cancels the comparison factors. This gives the first equation for arbitrary a, rather than only an isomorphism or a single evaluation.

proof.text: The completed-to-ordinary pullback, support realization, and canonical proper/open Frobenius maps of [def-pur-field-geometric-comparison-data] are natural transformations. Their composite integralExchange is natural. Conjugate this naturality square by the specified integralLeft natural isomorphism of the coefficient system and lift through the faithful finite-Tor inclusion in [def-pur-weil-equivariance-data]. This is exactly naturality of integralBeta.

theorem integralEquivariance_naturality :
    (∀ {K L : finiteTorConstructibleIntegralCategory P.coefficients.l P.extension
        (P.frobeniusFiber Y₀).left} (a : K ⟶ L),
      (integralGamma P X₀ Y₀ f₀ d c₀ S K).hom ≫
          (S.ring.operation (zlGeometricCompactification P.field f₀ c₀)
            (.integral (AdicSmoothDualizing.fieldStage P))).G.map a =
        (integralH P (P.frobeniusMap f₀) d).map a ≫
          (integralGamma P X₀ Y₀ f₀ d c₀ S L).hom) ∧
    (∀ {M N : finiteTorConstructibleIntegralCategory P.coefficients.l P.extension
        (P.frobeniusFiber X₀).left} (a : M ⟶ N),
      (integralP P Y₀).map
          ((S.ring.operation (zlGeometricCompactification P.field f₀ c₀)
            (.integral (AdicSmoothDualizing.fieldStage P))).F.map a) ≫
        (integralBeta P X₀ Y₀ f₀ c₀ S N).hom =
      (integralBeta P X₀ Y₀ f₀ c₀ S M).hom ≫
        (S.ring.operation (zlGeometricCompactification P.field f₀ c₀)
          (.integral (AdicSmoothDualizing.fieldStage P))).F.map ((integralP P X₀).map a))
